title: user-facing-latency-storyboards-and-telemetry-debt-register
content:
Goal: capture a product-centric view of latency (perceived + backend) and produce a prioritized, actionable telemetry debt register + dashboard wireframes for Q2 observability sprint.

Context / motivation:
- Engineering and product teams keep surfacing "app feels slow" issues. Backend p95 alone doesn't explain user experience because of client rendering, SDK batching, network hops, and retry/backoff behavior.
- We need a small, high-impact telemetry surface that ties a user-visible latency story ("time-to-first-token" / "time-to-complete") to backend spans and budgeted SLIs so incidents and rollouts are diagnosable by product teams.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Definitions for 4 user-facing latency SLI slices: TTFToken (time-to-first-token), TTCompletion (time-to-last-token), PerceivedLatency (client-side render), and EndToEnd90 (full roundtrip 90th quantile including SDK).
- Required backend metric mappings and trace anchors to locate cold-cache / kv-cache-eviction / batching hotspots.
- Sampling and trace-enrichment guidance (tenant tags, route, model-version).
- Dashboard wireframes (low-fidelity textual sketches) and alerting knobs.
- Telemetry debt register: list of missing signals, owners, estimated work, and priority.

Definitions (proposed):
1) TTFToken_user_sli: time from client request create_ts to first token emitted to client SDK.
   - Source: client SDK timing header + server span 'emit.first_token' anchor.
   - Unit: ms, SLI: p95, SLO candidate: 200ms p95 for hosted-tier; 150ms for dedicated.
2) TTCompletion_user_sli: time from request create_ts to final token emitted (end-of-stream).
   - Source: SDK end event or streaming finish event; server span 'session.complete'.
   - Unit: ms, SLI: p95, SLO candidate: 800ms p95 for short responses (<256 tokens).
3) PerceivedLatency_index: measured client-side time from "prompt injected" to first visible token (approx rendering).
   - Source: synthetic browser probes + SDK telemetry.
   - Use cases: detect client render regressions independent of server.
4) EndToEnd90: full roundtrip including network, SDK retry, and backoff (p90).

Backend metric mappings (what to instrument):
- span.duration:emit.first_token (server span) -> anchor to TTFToken (already exists but missing tenant tag in 27% of traces).
- batch.size.histogram per route/model -> correlate with latency and token cost.
- kvcache.hit_ratio per model_version + tenant -> needed to explain cold-cache TTF spikes.
- compile/kernels/quantize_time external metric (ms) -> long tail contributor for some model variants.
- socket.queue.time and accept-to-first-byte for edge proxies -> helps differentiate network vs runtime.

Trace enrichment and sampling:
- Mandatory attributes to add on request traces: tenant_id, route_id, model_version, request_id, sdk_version, credential_tier. Keep attribute list short to avoid high-cardinality.
- Adaptive sampling policy: sample 100% of traces with duration > p95 for any of the TTFToken/TTCompletion metrics for a route (capture failures and long-tails). Sample 1% of normal traces for baseline metrics.
- Retain full traces for traces marked by synthetic probes or alert hits for 7 days; aggregated traces for 30 days.

Dashboard wireframes (textual):
A) "User Latency Storyboard" (top row)
  - Left: small matrix of TTFToken p50/p95/p99 per route (sparkline 7d).
  - Center: TTCompletion p50/p95 with bucketed response length overlay.
  - Right: PerceivedLatency from synthetic probes vs client SDK (two lines).
  - Drilldown link: open trace sampling list filtered to "slow TTFToken" (with tenant filter).
B) "Backend Attribution" (middle row)
  - Waterfall breakdown: proxy time | load-balancer | runtime scheduling | kv-cache miss penalty | model-compile time | emit time. Use stacked bars with average and p95 overlays.
  - Heatmap: batch size vs TTFToken p95 for top 10 routes.
C) "Telemetry Health" (bottom row)
  - Missing tags gauge (count of spans missing tenant_id per day).
  - Trace sampling budget usage (quota left for the week).
  - Telemetry debt register snapshot (top 5 items).

Alerting and guardrails:
- Primary alert: increase in TTFToken p95 by 25% over 1h vs baseline (auto-derive baseline from 14d median). Fire to eng-oncall with route and top 3 contributors from waterfall attribution.
- Secondary alert: kv-cache hit_ratio drop > 10% absolute for a model_version for 15m. Pager to model-ops.
- Telemetry alert: missing tenant tag rate > 5% of traces -> page obs-instrumentation rotation.

Telemetry debt register (initial):
- TD-1: missing tenant_id in SDK server spans (owner: devx-sdks, estimate: 2d, priority: P0)
- TD-2: no streaming-first-token event in old legacy proxy (owner: infra-edge, estimate: 3d, priority: P1)
- TD-3: batch size histogram not emitted for dedicated nodes (owner: serving-runtime, estimate: 4d, priority: P1)
- TD-4: no kvcache.hit_ratio per tenant for on-prem deployments (owner: private-deployments, estimate: 5d, priority: P2)
- TD-5: synthetic probe coverage missing for APAC regions (owner: sre, estimate: 2d, priority: P2)

Quick implementation plan (next 6 weeks):
- Week 0-1: add tenant_id enrichment to SDK and server spans + deploy low-cardinality runtime tag scrubber. Create JIRA tickets (CONFLUENCE-OBS-1024 referenced).
- Week 2: emit batch.size histograms and hook into dashboard heatmaps.
- Week 3: add first-token synthetic probe to browser/SDK harness for top 5 routes.
- Week 4: wire up waterfall attribution panels and implement simple runbook generator that attaches top-3 suspected causes to incidents.
- Week 5-6: migrate sampling policy to adaptive rules and run a 2-week canary.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How much cardinality can we tolerate for model_version? We avoid free-form version strings; prefer normalized version tags.
- Storage cost vs retention: full-trace retention for slow traces is valuable for root cause but expensive. Proposed compromise: keep full traces for 7 days and aggregated indexed summaries for 90 days.
- Should perceived latency live in the same dashboard as backend attribution or a separate product-facing view? Leaning to combined for initial rollout to help cross-team debugging.

Action items (owners):
- Priya: file the infra-edge legacy proxy ticket and coordinate SDK change (due 2025-02-21).
- Evan: prototype waterfall bar builder and sample SQL for attribution (due 2025-02-25).
- Marisol: design a compact dashboard layout and share Figma wireframes (due 2025-02-28).
- Ravi: add adaptive sampling rule draft and run small simulation (due 2025-02-26).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic — the goal is an MVP that reduces time-to-diagnosis. Expect followups on normalization of model_version and telemetry cost budgeting. Please add missing debt items and tag owners inline in the doc.

Revision history:
